docs.title: Stable Diffusion (Local)
docs.text: Best for: Full control, privacy, fine-tuning, no API costs

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
• SDXL 1.0 — Best quality, 1024x1024 native
  • SD 1.5 — Faster, huge ecosystem of fine-tunes
  • SDXL Turbo — 1-4 steps, real-time generation
  • SD 3.5 — Latest, improved text rendering

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• GPU: 8GB+ VRAM (12GB+ recommended for SDXL)
  • CUDA 11.8+ or ROCm for AMD
  • Python 3.10+

docs.title: Setup (Diffusers)
docs.text: pip install diffusers transformers accelerate torch

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
import torch
from diffusers import StableDiffusionXLPipeline

pipe = StableDiffusionXLPipeline.from_pretrained(
    "stabilityai/stable-diffusion-xl-base-1.0",
    torch_dtype=torch.float16
)
pipe.to("cuda")

image = pipe(
    prompt="A majestic lion in a field of flowers",
    negative_prompt="blurry, low quality, distorted",
    num_inference_steps=30,
    guidance_scale=7.5,
    width=1024,
    height=1024
).images[0]

image.save("lion.png")

docs.title: Key Parameters
docs.text:
• num_inference_steps — Quality vs speed (20-50)
  • guidance_scale — Prompt adherence (5-15, default 7.5)
  • negative_prompt — What to avoid
  • seed — Reproducibility via generator=torch.Generator().manual_seed(N)

docs.title: img2img (Image Editing)
docs.text:
from diffusers import StableDiffusionXLImg2ImgPipeline

pipe = StableDiffusionXLImg2ImgPipeline.from_pretrained(...)
image = pipe(
    prompt="A painting in impressionist style",
    image=init_image,
    strength=0.5,  # 0=no change, 1=full regeneration
).images[0]

docs.title: Inpainting
docs.text:
from diffusers import StableDiffusionXLInpaintPipeline

pipe = StableDiffusionXLInpaintPipeline.from_pretrained(...)
image = pipe(
    prompt="A cat sitting on the couch",
    image=init_image,
    mask_image=mask,  # White = inpaint, black = keep
).images[0]

docs.title: Web UIs
docs.text:
• ComfyUI — Node-based, powerful workflows
  • Automatic1111 — Feature-rich, extensions
  • Fooocus — Simple, Midjourney-like experience

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Use LoRAs for specific styles/characters
  • VAE affects color saturation
  • Higher steps ≠ always better (diminishing returns after 30-40)

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text: Use when the main artifact is a Microsoft PowerPoint presentation or .pptx deck, especially when layouts, templates, placeholders, notes, comments, charts, extraction, editing, or final visual quality matter.

docs.title: AI Integration Landscape
docs.text:
Platform Integration Use When Plus AI Native PowerPoint/Google Slides add-in Need AI generation inside existing PPTX workflow Microsoft Copilot Built into Microsoft 365 Already on M365, need document→deck conversion Gamma Web-first card-based export Rapid prototyping, then export to PPTX for polish Beautiful.ai Rule-based auto-layout Design consistency is top priority Canva Magic Design + PPTX export Need large asset library + AI generation

Key insight: In 2026, the optimal workflow often = AI generation (Gamma/Copilot) → PPTX export → manual QA/polish in PowerPoint.

docs.title: 🆕 Async-First Awareness
docs.text:
Most decks are now shared asynchronously via email/Teams/WeChat without a presenter.

QA checklist for async-ready decks: - [ ] Can every slide be understood independently without a speaker? - [ ] Are all slide titles complete conclusion sentences (not descriptive phrases)? - [ ] Do charts have self-explanatory annotations/labels? - [ ] Are Speaker Notes filled for every slide (they are the "hidden narration")? - [ ] Is body text ≥18pt for mobile readability? - [ ] Are multi-column layouts avoided on content-rich slides?

docs.title: 🆕 Gamma Card-Based Thinking
docs.text: The "card" mental model (from Gamma's dominance): - Each slide = one independent card/module - Cards can be reordered, skipped, or expanded without breaking the narrative - Traditional linear slides → modular card decks for flexible presentations - When editing existing decks: consider if rigid linear order could benefit from modular restructuring

docs.title: 🆕 Mobile + Export Awareness
docs.text:
• PPTX shared via links → opened on phones increasingly common
  • Export to PDF → check mobile rendering
  • Complex animations/transitions → often lost in export/conversion
  • Font substitution across platforms → test on target devices

docs.title: Core Rules (保持，略)
docs.text: (Same 6 rules from v1.0.1)

docs.title: 🆕 2026 Common Traps (新增)
docs.text:
• AI-generated decks from Gamma/Copilot often look polished but break on PPTX export — always verify layout after import
  • Async-shared decks with incomplete Speaker Notes lose 40%+ of intended information
  • Mobile viewers can't read body text below 16pt — 2026 standard is 18pt minimum
  • AI-generated images may have inconsistent styles across slides — establish image style guidelines before generation
  • Card-based layouts export poorly to traditional PPTX if not explicitly designed for both formats
  • Copilot-generated speaker notes can be verbose; trim to key points only

Mitigation: Inventory layouts, placeholders, masters, charts, notes, comments, and media before editing, then verify affected slides after each change. Mitigation: Run content QA and rendered visual QA separately, including at least one fix-and-verify pass for layout-sensitive decks.

docs.text: 将论文一键转化为：翻译稿 + 总结 + PPT + 演讲稿全套物料，自动发送到微信

docs.title: 🎯 简介
docs.text:
学术汇报全自动化是一个端到端的论文处理工作流。只需提供论文（PDF 或文本），即可自动生成：

  • 📄 翻译稿（Word .docx）— 论文全文中文翻译
  • 📄 总结稿（Word .docx）— 核心框架结构化总结
  • 📊 PPT 演示文稿（.pptx）— 10-15 页汇报幻灯片
  • 📝 逐字演讲稿（Markdown）— 每页配套口语化讲解

所有文件完成后自动发送到你的微信。

docs.title: ✨ 核心特性
docs.text: 特性 说明 🚀 全自动化 6 个阶段自动衔接，一键启动 📱 微信通知 PPT 生成后自动发送到微信，无需手动下载 📝 Word 输出 翻译稿和总结稿直接输出为可编辑 .docx 文件 🎨 智能 PPT 调用外部 PPT 生成 API，自动设计 10-15 页专业幻灯片 🔒 安全私密 API Key 由用户自行配置，不嵌入任何密钥 🌍 通用平台 支持 anygen、gamma.app 等多种 PPT API

docs.text:

docs.text:

clawhub install academic-presentation

# 方式 2：手动复制
cp -r academic-presentation/ ~/.openclaw/skills/

docs.title: 首次配置 PPT 平台
docs.text:
首次触发时，技能会询问选择 PPT 生成平台：

请选择 PPT 生成方式：
1. anygen（推荐）- 需要 ANYGEN_API_KEY
2. gamma.app - 需要 GAMMA_API_KEY  
3. 跳过 PPT - 仅生成 Word 和演讲稿

选择后，输入对应的 API Key 即可。

docs.title: 支持的 PPT API
docs.text: 平台 API Key 环境变量 注册地址 特点 anygen.io ANYGEN_API_KEY https://www.anygen.io 中文支持好，推荐学术使用 gamma.app GAMMA_API_KEY https://gamma.app 国际通用 跳过 无 — 仅生成文档和讲稿

docs.title: Stage 1：接收文档
docs.text: 提供论文 PDF 文件路径或直接粘贴论文文本，系统自动： - 提取论文标题 - 识别语言（中文/英文/其他） - 设定工作变量 [Doc_Title]

docs.title: Stage 2：核心内容翻译（可选）
docs.text:
将论文核心内容（摘要、引言、方法、实验、结论）翻译为流畅的中文学术语言，输出为 Word 文档。

输出：/tmp/academic-ppt/[论文标题]_翻译稿.docx

docs.title: Stage 3：论文精要总结
docs.text:
提炼论文核心框架，输出为结构化 Word 文档：

  1. 研究背景与痛点 (Motivation)
  2. 核心贡献 (Contributions)
  3. 方法与架构 (Methodology)
  4. 实验结果 (Experiments)
  5. 结论与局限 (Conclusion)

输出：/tmp/academic-ppt/[论文标题]_总结.docx

docs.title: Stage 4：PPT 大纲设计
docs.text: 根据总结自动设计 10-15 页汇报大纲，每页包含： - 标题 - 核心要点（3-5 个） - 过渡句设计

docs.title: Stage 5：PPT 生成
docs.text:
调用你选择的 PPT API 生成专业演示文稿：

输出：/tmp/academic-ppt/*.pptx

⚠️ PPT 生成可能需要 1-5 分钟，请耐心等待

docs.title: Stage 6：逐字演讲稿
docs.text:
根据 PPT 每页内容，撰写配套口语化逐字稿，包含： - 开场白和过渡句 - 每页讲解内容 - 总结和致谢

输出：/tmp/academic-ppt/speech_notes.md

docs.title: Stage 7：微信自动发送（🎉亮点）
docs.text:
所有文件生成完成后，自动通过微信发送给你：

  • 📄 翻译稿（.docx）
  • 📄 总结稿（.docx）
  • 📊 PPT（.pptx）
  • 📝 演讲稿（.md）

无需手动下载，文件直接出现在微信！

docs.title: 学术汇报全自动化 v4.0
docs.text: 将论文转化为包含翻译、总结、PPT及演讲稿的全套物料。 v4.0: 2026前沿趋势注入——Async-First独立阅读设计、AI学术图像生成、移动端适配、暖色极简美学。

docs.title: v4.0.0 更新
docs.text:
• 🆕 Async-First设计：学术PPT=独立文档，无讲解者也传达完整信息
  • 🆕 移动端适配：学术报告越来越多在手机上审阅
  • 🆕 AI学术图像生成：通过Copilot/AI描述生成定制化学术插图
  • 🆕 暖色极简学术风格：暖色调+柔和形状取代冷白色学术背景
  • 🆕 Gamma卡片式思维：模块化内容块, 灵活重组讲解节奏
  • ✅ 继承v3.0所有：3种叙事框架、图表优先、证据等级、答辩节奏

docs.title: 原则0: Async-First（独立可读性）⭐ 最重要
docs.text:
在2026年，大多数学术PPT通过邮件/微信/Teams分享，审阅者在没有你的讲解下阅读。

要求： - 每张slide即使脱离演讲者，也能独力传达该页的核心信息 - 标题必须是完整结论句，而非描述性短语 - 图表必须配自解释标注（annotation），不依赖口头说明 - Speaker Notes 强制填写（异步阅读者的"隐藏解说"）

自检：把PPT发给导师，不加任何说明，ta能完全理解吗？

docs.title: 原则1: 图表优先（Figure-First Design）
docs.text:
• Methods 页用流程图替代纯文字
  • Results 页用图表+annotation替代表格罗列
  • 每张图表配1条「关键发现」标注文字（≤15字）

docs.title: 原则2: 15字学术标题法则
docs.text:
• 标题 = 该页的核心发现/结论
  • ❌ "实验结果分析" → ✅ "模型A在3个数据集上优于baseline"
  • ❌ "相关工作" → ✅ "现有方法均未解决跨域泛化问题"

docs.title: 原则3: 证据等级标注
docs.text:
• 在PPT的关键结论旁标注证据等级
  • [Established] / [Comparative] / [Computational] / [Speculative]

docs.title: 原则4: 知识缺口诚实标记
docs.text:
• 至少2页主动展示研究局限
  • 避免"完美研究"假象

docs.title: 🆕 原则5: 移动端优先
docs.text:
正文最小字号: 18pt (手机上可读)
图表标签最小: 14pt
避免密集多列布局: 手机屏宽≈375px
高对比度: 户外/通勤场景也能看清

docs.title: 🆕 原则6: AI学术图像生成
docs.text:
学术插图: Copilot/Gemini/DALL-E生成定制化概念图
化学结构/分子: AI生成3D分子模型
数据可视化升级: AI辅助选择最佳图表类型
提示词模板: "科学插图风格，展示[概念]，简洁线条，学术配色，白底，适合期刊发表"

docs.title: 框架D: 模块化卡片（Gamma风格）🆕
docs.text:
适用于：在线预讲、异步分享、灵活组会

核心卡片(1张) → 问题卡片(1-2张) → 方法卡片(2-3张)
→ 结果卡片(2-3张) → 局限卡片(1张) → 展望卡片(1张)
  • 每张卡片 = 1个独立论点
  • 可自由排序, 按听众兴趣跳过/深入
  • 适合网络分享和异步审阅

docs.title: 🟢 Stage 4：PPT大纲设计（升级版）
docs.text:
输出格式（v4.0升级）：

### Slide 1: 标题页（≤15字标题 + 作者信息 + 日期）
🎯 核心信息：一句话概括整个研究
📱 移动自检：标题在手机上清晰可读

### Slide 2: 问题背景
🎯 核心信息：[一个背景陈述]
📊 视觉：关键数据大字卡
💡 One Idea：为什么这个问题值得研究？
📝 Speaker Note：[异步阅读者需要的背景补充]

### Slide 3-5: 方法/发现（图表优先 + 自解释标注）
📊 每页1个核心图/表 + 1条Key Finding标注
📝 Speaker Note：[方法细节补充]

### Slide N-2: 知识缺口（诚实页）
🎯 核心信息：[具体局限1]
🎯 核心信息：[具体局限2]
💡 "这些局限意味着..."

### Slide N: 致谢/QA

🆕 Async-First自检表： - [ ] 去掉Speaker Notes, 每页能否独立理解? - [ ] 图表标注是否自解释? - [ ] 手机上正文≥18pt是否可读? - [ ] 配色是否通过WCAG AA对比度?

docs.text: 检查给定期刊是否被 SCI（Science Citation Index）或 SSCI（Social Sciences Citation Index）索引。

docs.title: 使用场景
docs.text: 在论文质量评估流程中： 1. 判断文章类型 → 预印本？→ 直接 PaperClaw 2. 非预印本 → 检查期刊是否在 SCI/SSCI → 通过后 → PaperClaw

docs.title: 数据来源
docs.text:
• Web of Science (WoS)
  • Journal Citation Reports (JCR)
  • 更新频率：每年一次

docs.title: 期刊列表文件
docs.text:
• 路径：/workspace/skills/journal-sci-ssci-checker/data/journals.txt
  • 格式：每行一个期刊名（支持模糊匹配）

docs.title: 输入
docs.text: • 期刊名称（journal_name）

docs.title: 处理逻辑
docs.text:
1. 加载期刊列表（journals.txt）
  2. 模糊匹配输入的期刊名
  3. 返回匹配结果：
  4. SCI - 被 SCI 索引
  5. SSCI - 被 SSCI 索引
  6. BOTH - 同时被 SCI 和 SSCI 索引
  7. NOT_FOUND - 不在列表中

docs.title: 输出
docs.text:
{
  "journal_name": "输入的期刊名",
  "matched_name": "匹配到的期刊名",
  "indexed_in": ["SCI", "SSCI"],
  "result": "PASS" | "FAIL"
}

docs.title: 示例
docs.text:
输入：

Journal of Personality and Social Psychology

输出：

{
  "journal_name": "Journal of Personality and Social Psychology",
  "matched_name": "Journal of Personality and Social Psychology",
  "indexed_in": ["SCI", "SSCI"],
  "result": "PASS"
}

docs.title: 更新期刊列表
docs.text:
运行更新脚本：

python3 /workspace/skills/journal-sci-ssci-checker/scripts/update_journals.py

该脚本会： 1. 从 Web of Science 获取最新期刊列表 2. 更新 JCR 数据 3. 合并去重 4. 保存到 journals.txt

docs.title: 注意事项
docs.text:
• 预印本文章不需要执行此检查
  • 建议每年更新一次期刊列表
  • 匹配采用模糊匹配（忽略大小写、空格差异）

docs.text:

This skill is ready for commercial/non-commercial use.

docs.title: Use Case:
docs.text: Researchers, reviewers, and corpus builders use this skill to check whether a non-preprint psychology journal appears in a local SCI/SSCI journal list before downstream paper quality assessment.

docs.title: Deployment Geography for Use:

docs.title: Known Risks and Mitigations:
docs.text: Risk: The bundled journal list can become stale or incomplete relative to official SCI/SSCI records. Mitigation: Confirm consequential journal-status decisions directly in official Web of Science or Journal Citation Reports sources and update the local list on a regular review cycle. Risk: Fuzzy journal-title matching can select the wrong journal when titles are abbreviated, renamed, or similar. Mitigation: Review the matched journal name and index classification before relying on a PASS or FAIL result.

docs.title: 原则 0: Async-First ⭐ 2026 Most Important
docs.text:
Most HTML decks are shared as links — no presenter alongside.

  • Every slide title = complete conclusion sentence
  • Charts/diagrams must have self-explanatory annotations
  • Optional "Speaker Note" collapsible area at slide bottom
  • Goal: send the HTML link to anyone → they fully understand

docs.title: 原则 1: Warm Minimalism 🆕
docs.text:
• White → warm cream/light gray backgrounds
  • Pure black → warm dark gray text
  • Cool blue → warm amber/coral accent colors
  • Soft shadows, rounded corners, organic shapes
.warm-minimal {
    --bg: #FAF7F2;
    --text: #3D3929;
    --accent: #E07A5F;
    --card-bg: #FFF9F0;
    --shadow: 0 2px 12px rgba(61,57,41,0.08);

docs.title: 原则 2: Card-Based Layout (Gamma-inspired) 🆕
docs.text:
.card-deck {
    display: grid;
    grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(280px, 1fr));
    gap: 1.5rem;
}
.card {
    background: var(--card-bg);
    border-radius: 16px;
    padding: 2rem;
    transition: transform 0.3s ease;
}
.card:hover { transform: translateY(-4px); }

docs.title: 原则 3: 3D CSS Effects 🆕
docs.text:

    .card-deck { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }
    .title { font-size: 1.5rem; }
    .two-column { flex-direction: column; }

docs.text: Risk: The skill can read presentation files and image folders provided by the user. Mitigation: Use it only in trusted OpenClaw environments and avoid sensitive decks or assets unless the environment is approved for that data. Risk: PowerPoint conversion and image processing may require installing python-pptx and Pillow from PyPI. Mitigation: Review dependency installation commands before running them and use a managed Python environment where package installation is allowed. Risk: Generated or converted slide content may preserve confidential source material in output files. Mitigation: Review generated HTML and extracted assets before sharing or publishing the deck.

docs.title: Style Presets Reference
docs.text: Curated visual styles for Frontend Slides. Each preset is inspired by real design references—no generic "AI slop" aesthetics. Abstract shapes only—no illustrations.

docs.title: ⚠️ CRITICAL: Viewport Fitting (Non-Negotiable)
docs.text: Every slide MUST fit exactly in the viewport. No scrolling within slides, ever.

docs.title: Content Density Limits Per Slide
docs.text:
Slide Type Maximum Content Title slide 1 heading + 1 subtitle Content slide 1 heading + 4-6 bullets (max 2 lines each) Feature grid 1 heading + 6 cards (2x3 or 3x2) Code slide 1 heading + 8-10 lines of code Quote slide 1 quote (max 3 lines) + attribution

Too much content? → Split into multiple slides. Never scroll.

docs.title: Required Base CSS (Include in ALL Presentations)
docs.text:
/* ===========================================
   VIEWPORT FITTING: MANDATORY
   Copy this entire block into every presentation
   =========================================== */

/* 1. Lock document to viewport */
html, body {
    height: 100%;
    overflow-x: hidden;
}

html {
    scroll-snap-type: y mandatory;
    scroll-behavior: smooth;
}

/* 2. Each slide = exact viewport height */
.slide {
    width: 100vw;
    height: 100vh;
    height: 100dvh; /* Dynamic viewport for mobile */
    overflow: hidden; /* CRITICAL: No overflow ever */
    scroll-snap-align: start;
    display: flex;
    flex-direction: column;
    position: relative;
}

/* 3. Content wrapper */
.slide-content {
    flex: 1;
    display: flex;
    flex-direction: column;
    justify-content: center;
    max-height: 100%;
    overflow: hidden;
    padding: var(--slide-padding);
}

/* 4. ALL sizes use clamp() - scales with viewport */
:root {
    /* Typography */
    --title-size: clamp(1.5rem, 5vw, 4rem);
    --h2-size: clamp(1.25rem, 3.5vw, 2.5rem);
    --body-size: clamp(0.75rem, 1.5vw, 1.125rem);
    --small-size: clamp(0.65rem, 1vw, 0.875rem);

    /* Spacing */
    --slide-padding: clamp(1rem, 4vw, 4rem);
    --content-gap: clamp(0.5rem, 2vw, 2rem);
}

/* 5. Cards/containers use viewport-relative max sizes */
.card, .container {
    max-width: min(90vw, 1000px);
    max-height: min(80vh, 700px);
}

/* 6. Images constrained */
img {
    max-width: 100%;
    max-height: min(50vh, 400px);
    object-fit: contain;
}

/* 7. Grids adapt to space */
.grid {
    display: grid;
    grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, 220px), 1fr));
    gap: clamp(0.5rem, 1.5vw, 1rem);
}

/* ===========================================
   RESPONSIVE BREAKPOINTS - Height-based
   =========================================== */

/* Short screens (< 700px height) */
@media (max-height: 700px) {
    :root {
        --slide-padding: clamp(0.75rem, 3vw, 2rem);
        --content-gap: clamp(0.4rem, 1.5vw, 1rem);
        --title-size: clamp(1.25rem, 4.5vw, 2.5rem);
    }
}

/* Very short (< 600px height) */
@media (max-height: 600px) {
    :root {
        --slide-padding: clamp(0.5rem, 2.5vw, 1.5rem);
        --title-size: clamp(1.1rem, 4vw, 2rem);
        --body-size: clamp(0.7rem, 1.2vw, 0.95rem);
    }

    .nav-dots, .keyboard-hint, .decorative {
        display: none;
    }
}

/* Extremely short - landscape phones (< 500px) */
@media (max-height: 500px) {
    :root {
        --slide-padding: clamp(0.4rem, 2vw, 1rem);
        --title-size: clamp(1rem, 3.5vw, 1.5rem);
        --body-size: clamp(0.65rem, 1vw, 0.85rem);
    }
}

/* Narrow screens */
@media (max-width: 600px) {
    .grid {
        grid-template-columns: 1fr;
    }
}

/* Reduced motion */
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
    *, *::before, *::after {
        animation-duration: 0.01ms !important;
        transition-duration: 0.2s !important;
    }
}

docs.title: Viewport Fitting Checklist
docs.text:
Before finalizing any presentation, verify:

  • [ ] Every .slide has height: 100vh; height: 100dvh; overflow: hidden;
  • [ ] All font sizes use clamp(min, preferred, max)
  • [ ] All spacing uses clamp() or viewport units
  • [ ] Breakpoints exist for heights: 700px, 600px, 500px
  • [ ] Content respects density limits (max 6 bullets, max 6 cards)
  • [ ] No fixed pixel heights on content elements
  • [ ] Images have max-height constraints
  • [ ] No negated CSS functions (use calc(-1 * clamp(...)) not -clamp(...))

docs.title: Negating CSS Functions
docs.text:
WRONG — silently ignored by browsers:

right: -clamp(28px, 3.5vw, 44px);   /* ❌ Invalid! Browser ignores this */
margin-left: -min(10vw, 100px);      /* ❌ Invalid! */
top: -max(2rem, 4vh);                /* ❌ Invalid! */

CORRECT — wrap in calc():

right: calc(-1 * clamp(28px, 3.5vw, 44px));  /* ✅ */
margin-left: calc(-1 * min(10vw, 100px));     /* ✅ */
top: calc(-1 * max(2rem, 4vh));               /* ✅ */

CSS does not allow a leading - before function names like clamp(), min(), max(). The browser silently discards the entire declaration, causing the property to fall back to its initial/inherited value. This is especially dangerous because there is no console error — the element simply appears in the wrong position.

Rule: Always use calc(-1 * ...) to negate CSS function values.

docs.title: Content Overflows the Slide
docs.text:
Symptoms: Scrollbar appears, content cut off, elements outside viewport

Solutions: 1. Check slide has overflow: hidden (not overflow: auto or visible) 2. Reduce content — split into multiple slides 3. Ensure all fonts use clamp() not fixed px or rem 4. Add/fix height breakpoints for smaller screens 5. Check images have max-height: min(50vh, 400px)

docs.title: Text Too Small on Mobile / Too Large on Desktop
docs.text:
Symptoms: Unreadable text on phones, oversized text on big screens

Solutions:

/* Use clamp with viewport-relative middle value */
font-size: clamp(1rem, 3vw, 2.5rem);
/*              ↑       ↑      ↑
            minimum  scales  maximum */

docs.title: Content Doesn't Fill Short Screens
docs.text:
Symptoms: Excessive whitespace on landscape phones or short browser windows

Solutions: 1. Add @media (max-height: 600px) and (max-height: 500px) breakpoints 2. Reduce padding at smaller heights 3. Hide decorative elements (display: none) 4. Consider hiding nav dots and hints on short screens

docs.title: Testing Recommendations
docs.text:
Test at these viewport sizes: - Desktop: 1920×1080, 1440×900, 1280×720 - Tablet: 1024×768 (landscape), 768×1024 (portrait) - Mobile: 375×667 (iPhone SE), 414×896 (iPhone 11) - Landscape phone: 667×375, 896×414

Use browser DevTools responsive mode to quickly test multiple sizes.

docs.title: 中文学术论文写作助手 v2.0
触发条件
docs.text: 当用户提及以下任何内容时激活： - 论文写作、学术论文、毕业论文、学位论文 - 开题报告、研究计划、研究提案 - 文献综述、文献回顾 - 期刊投稿、投稿准备 - 论文大纲、章节规划 - 学术写作、中文学术写作 - 引用格式、脚注、参考文献 - 2026新增：去AI味、降AI率、AI痕迹消除

docs.title: 1. 需求确认
docs.text: 首先明确用户当前所处的写作阶段： - 选题阶段：有初步想法但不确定方向 - 大纲阶段：需要规划论文结构 - 开题阶段：撰写开题报告/研究计划 - 写作阶段：正在写正文（某一章/节） - 去AI化阶段 🆕：已有初稿，需要消除AI写作痕迹 - 修改阶段：已有初稿，需要润色和检查 - 投稿阶段：准备投稿，需要格式调整

docs.title: 2. 加载对应规范
docs.text: 根据用户学科和需求，加载 references/ 中的对应文档： - citation-guide.md — 引用格式规范 - paper-structure.md — 论文章节结构指南 - proposal-template.md — 开题报告模板 - literature-review-guide.md — 文献综述写作指南 - de-ai-guide.md 🆕 — 中文AI痕迹检测与去AI化指南

docs.title: 选题与大纲
docs.text:
• 生成 2-3 个可行题目
  • 输出详细大纲（章-节-小节三级）
  • 标注每部分建议字数和核心论点

docs.title: 开题报告
docs.text: • 按模板输出：研究背景、文献回顾、研究问题、研究方法、章节安排、预期贡献

docs.title: 文献综述
docs.text:
• 帮助梳理论争脉络
  • 识别研究空白（research gap）
  • 绝不编造文献内容

docs.title: 正文写作
docs.text:
• 逐章/逐节辅助
  • 2026新增写作原则：
  • ❌ 避免"首先...其次...再次...最后"线性罗列 → 改用嵌套论证
  • ❌ 避免段落以"本文通过/本章将/本研究旨在"开头 ≥3次
  • ✅ 段落首句多样化（问题驱动、对比驱动、材料驱动）

docs.title: 🆕 去AI化处理（2026新增核心功能）
中文AI痕迹识别清单
docs.text:
🔴 高危模板（需全部清除）：

模板 替换建议 "具有重要意义" / "具有重要的理论意义和现实意义" 删除或改为具体说明对哪方面有意义 "本文通过...研究...得出...结论" 改为自然叙述，如"基于X的分析，我们发现Y" "为...提供了新的思路/视角/方法" 具体说明提供了什么，而非泛化表态 "随着...的发展/深入/推进" 删除或替换为具体时间节点/事件 "不仅...而且..." 每3000字限1次 "在一定程度上" / "在某种意义上" 替换为具体限定条件 "众所周知" / "毋庸置疑" / "不可否认" 删除，直接陈述事实或引用来源

🟡 中危模式（每3000字限1-2次）：

模式 检测方法 段首以"首先/其次/再次/最后"开头 全文零容忍 结论段以"综上所述/总而言之/由上可知"开头 替换为自然过渡 每段都是"总-分-总"结构 至少30%段落打破此模式 "的"字短语堆砌 ≥3层 拆分或简化 连续使用"进行+动词"（如"进行分析""进行讨论"） 直接用动词"分析""讨论"

🟢 句式多样性指标：

指标 AI文本 人类文本 达标线 句长标准差（字符数） < 8 > 12 ≥ 10 逗号密度（每100字逗号数） 8-10（过于均匀） 波动在3-15 标准差 > 3 段落开头词多样性 重复率 > 40% 重复率 < 20% < 25% "的"字密度 > 6% 3-5% < 5.5% 四字成语/固定搭配密度 2-3%（过高） 1-2% < 2.5%

docs.title: 中文去AI味执行流程
docs.text:
Step 1: 快速扫描 - 通读全文，标记上述🔴模板 - 统计句长分布和段落开头词 - 输出「AI痕迹热力图」：高亮AI痕迹集中的段落

Step 2: 句长重塑 - 中文理想句长分布：短句(5-15字)占15%，中句(15-35字)占60%，长句(35-60字)占25% - 连续3句长度差 < 5字 → 改写其中一句 - 段落结尾句倾向于短句收束

Step 3: 论证非线性化 - 检测"首先→其次→再次→最后" → 替换为嵌套论证结构 - 加入"需要指出的是""值得留意的是""反过来说"等转折/让步连接词 - 关键论证前插入1处"不完全确定性"表述 - 每5000字嵌入至少1处"策略性自反"：对自身论证方法的局限进行简短自省

Step 4: 学术习语注入 - 根据学科替换通用表达为学科习语： - 历史学：嵌入"揆诸""考辨""发覆""推原""这一判断值得商榷"等学科惯用语 - 哲学：嵌入"质言之""析而论之""进而言之""此一问题关涉..." - 文学：嵌入"细读之下""文本肌理""值得玩味的是""这一书写策略" - 人文学科使用主观判断句（限1次/2000字）： - "这一点尤其值得重视" - "这或许是最关键的差异所在" - "令人玩味的是"

Step 5: 知识缺口信号 - 在引言末尾标记1-2个研究界未解决的问题（具体而非泛化） - 在结论/余论部分诚实地指出本研究的边界 - 将"有待进一步研究"改为具体方向

Step 6: 策略性不完美 - 每8000字允许1处脚注中的"笔者对此尚无定论"式表述 - 论证中允许保留1-2处"这一现象的原因尚不明确" - 使用破折号插入补充说明（AI倾向于避免破折号）

docs.title: 润色与自检清单（2026升级版）
docs.text:
语言层面： - [ ] 消除口语化、冗余、模糊表达 - [ ] 🔴 模板清零（"具有重要意义""本文通过""综上所述"等） - [ ] 句长标准差 ≥ 10 - [ ] "的"字密度 < 5.5% - [ ] "进行+动词"模式无连续使用

逻辑层面： - [ ] 论证链条完整性 - [ ] 是否包含 ≥1 处让步/自我反驳 - [ ] 知识缺口信号 ≥2 处

格式层面： - [ ] 标题层级正确 - [ ] 标点规范（中文引号用「」或""，不用""） - [ ] 段落格式一致

引用层面： - [ ] 调用 cwphil-citation-style 检查脚注和参考文献格式合规性 - [ ] 所有引用都有出处，无抄袭风险 - [ ] 直接引用 vs 间接引用界限清晰

docs.title: 4. 输出规范
docs.text:
• 使用规范的学术中文
  • 重要术语首次出现时标注外文原文（如适用）
  • 段落清晰，每段有明确的主题句
  • 输出可复制粘贴的纯文本格式

docs.title: 核心原则
docs.text:
不编造原则： - 不虚构文献、不编造作者、不捏造页码 - 不编造研究数据、不捏造访谈内容 - 缺失信息明确标记 【待補：...】

学术诚信原则： - 提示用户正确引用 - 帮助改写和 paraphrase，而非直接复制

🆕 去AI化原则： - 目标是让文本"像人写的"，而非"看不出是AI写的" - 绝不是简单换词或加错误 - 保持学术严谨性的前提下注入人类写作特征 - 中文特有考量：文言/白话的自然混合、四字格适度使用、学科行话嵌入

docs.title: Description:
docs.text:
中文学术论文写作助手 supports Chinese academic paper workflows, including topic development, outlines, proposals, literature reviews, chapter drafting, citation formatting, polishing, and submission checks for humanities writing.

This skill is ready for commercial/non-commercial use.

docs.text: Students, researchers, and academic writers use this skill to draft and revise Chinese humanities papers, theses, proposals, and journal submissions while keeping citation and academic-integrity checks visible.

docs.title: Known Risks and Mitigations:
docs.text: Risk: Academic writing and citation guidance can still contain incorrect citation details, unsupported claims, or plagiarism-sensitive phrasing. Mitigation: Manually verify citations, bibliography fields, source boundaries, and final wording before academic submission. Risk: The skill references a companion cwphil-citation-style integration that is not included in this artifact. Mitigation: Review and install the companion skill separately before relying on automated citation formatting or citation self-checks.

docs.title: 《中國文哲研究集刊》撰稿格式規範
一、總則
docs.text: 本文獻引用格式適用於中文學術論著，涵蓋腳註與文末參考文獻兩大系統。

docs.title: 2.1 首次引用（完整格式）
docs.text:
專書：

作者名，《書名》（出版地：出版社，年份），頁碼。

例：余英時，《朱熹的歷史世界：宋代士大夫政治文化的研究》（臺北：允晨文化，2003），頁 25。

外文專書：

Author Name, Book Title (Place: Publisher, Year), pp. XX-XX.

例：Mark Edward Lewis, Writing and Authority in Early China (Albany: State University of New York Press, 1999), pp. 5-10.

期刊論文：

作者名，〈篇名〉，《期刊名》卷.期（年月），頁碼。

例：王汎森，〈思想史中的「思想」〉，《中央研究院歷史語言研究所集刊》75.1（2004.3），頁 1-28。

外文期刊：

Author Name, "Article Title," *Journal Name* Volume.Issue (Month Year): page range.

例：Joshua A. Fogel, "'Shanghai-Japan': The Japanese Residents' Association of Shanghai," Journal of Asian Studies 59.4 (Nov. 2000): 927-950.

論文集（書中篇章）：

作者名，〈篇名〉，收入編者名編，《書名》（出版地：出版社，年份），頁碼。

例：John C. Y. Wang, "Early Chinese Narrative: The Tso-chuan as Example," in Chinese Narrative: Critical and Theoretical Essays, ed. Andrew H. Plaks (Princeton: Princeton University Press, 1977), pp. 3-20.

學位論文：

作者名，《論文題目》（Ph.D. diss. / M.A. thesis, 學校名, 年份），頁碼。

例：Hwang Ming-chorng, "Mingtang: Cosmology, Political Order and Monuments in Early China" (Ph.D. diss., Harvard University, 1996), p. 20.

docs.title: 2.2 第二次引用（縮寫格式）
docs.text:
• 同一文獻第二次引用時，使用「同上」。
  • 若頁碼與前注不同，標註頁碼：「同上，頁 XX。」
  • 若頁碼與前注相同，只寫「同上。」

例：

同上，頁 33。

docs.title: 2.3 間隔引用（同註）
docs.text:
• 非連續引用同一文獻時，使用「同註[編號]，頁 XX。」
  • 若頁碼與該注相同，可省略頁碼。

例：

同註[3]，頁 45。

docs.title: 2.4 多作者引用
docs.text:
兩位作者：

作者甲、作者乙，《書名》...

三位及以上作者：

作者甲等，《書名》... 或 作者甲et al., Book Title...

docs.title: 2.5 重複引用同一位作者多篇著作
docs.text:
第二次引用同一作者不同著作時：

作者名，《書名》（見註[編號]），頁 XX。

或簡寫：

作者名，《書名》，頁 XX。

docs.title: 2.6 報紙引用
docs.text:
作者名，〈篇名〉，《報紙名》[出版地] 日期，版次，頁碼。

例：Michael A. Lev, "Nativity Signals Deep Roots for Christianity in China," Chicago Tribune [Chicago] 18 March 2008, Sec. 1, p. 4.

docs.title: 3.1 排序規則
docs.text:
• 按作者姓氏拼音（外文）或筆畫（中文）排序。
  • 無作者者按書名首字排序。
  • 同一作者按出版年份排序。

docs.title: 3.2 格式示例
docs.text:
中文專書：

余英時：《朱熹的歷史世界：宋代士大夫政治文化的研究》。臺北：允晨文化，2003。

外文專書：

Lewis, Mark Edward. Writing and Authority in Early China. Albany: State University of New York Press, 1999.

（注意：外文參考文獻採用姓名倒置，標點改為句點。）

期刊論文：

王汎森：〈思想史中的「思想」〉。《中央研究院歷史語言研究所集刊》75.1（2004.3）：1-28。

外文期刊：

Fogel, Joshua A. "'Shanghai-Japan': The Japanese Residents' Association of Shanghai." Journal of Asian Studies 59.4 (Nov. 2000): 927-950.

docs.title: 3.3 外文參考文獻特殊規則
docs.text:
• 作者姓名倒置：Last Name, First Name.
  • 書名改為斜體（以 * 標記）。
  • 刊名改為斜體。
  • 篇名加引號。
  • 標點符號從中文格式（頓號、書名號）改為英文格式（句點、逗號、引號）。

docs.title: 四、常見錯誤與修正
docs.text: 錯誤 正確 同上，頁 25-30（首次引用用同上） 首次引用必須用完整格式 余英時，《書名》，頁 25（缺少出版資訊） 余英時，《書名》（臺北：允晨文化，2003），頁 25。 同註 3（缺少頁碼且頁碼不同時） 同註[3]，頁 45。 Lewis, Mark Edward, Book Title...（外文參考文獻未倒置姓名） Lewis, Mark Edward. Book Title... 書名未用書名號《》 中文專書必須用《》，期刊用〈〉 頁碼寫成 "p. 25"（中文文獻） 中文用「頁 25」，外文用 "p. 25" 或 "pp. 25-30"

docs.title: 五、中英混排規則
docs.text:
• 中文正文夾雜外文時，外文詞組、書名、專有名詞保持原文，不翻譯。
  • 腳註中外文文獻完全按外文格式處理，不混入中文標點（除整句結構外）。
  • 參考文獻區分明確分類：中文文獻在前（按筆畫），外文文獻在後（按字母）。

docs.title: 腳註模板
docs.text:
[首次引用]
作者名，《書名》（出版地：出版社，年份），頁碼。

[第二次引用]
同上，頁碼。

[間隔引用]
同註[編號]，頁碼。

docs.title: 參考文獻模板
docs.text:
[中文]
作者名：《書名》。出版地：出版社，年份。

[外文]
Author Last Name, First Name. *Book Title*. Place: Publisher, Year.

docs.title: 一、文献综述不是「书单」
docs.text:
错误示范：

关于这个话题，A 研究了... B 研究了... C 研究了...

正确示范：

现有研究主要围绕三个维度展开：（一）...（二）...（三）...
其中，第一个维度的研究以 A 和 B 为代表，他们共同的看法是...，但在...问题上存在分歧...

核心原则：综述要呈现「学界对话」，而非「学者名单」。

docs.title: 二、文献综述的三种组织方式
方式一：按主题线索（最常用）
docs.text:
适用于：研究议题涉及多个侧面

结构：

现有研究主要从 N 个角度探讨了...问题：

（一）角度一的梳理
  - 代表学者及其观点
  - 该角度的贡献与局限

（二）角度二的梳理
  - ...

（三）角度三的梳理
  - ...

（四）现有研究的不足
  - 尚未关注的问题
  - 已有观点的盲点

示例：

关于《红楼梦》的研究，学界大致从三个维度展开：作者考证、文本阐释与文化意义。在作者考证方面，以胡适、周汝昌为代表的研究者通过文献考证，基本确定了曹雪芹的作者身份，但关于后四十回的作者问题仍无定论...

docs.title: 方式二：按时间脉络
docs.text:
适用于：议题有较清晰的发展阶段

结构：

关于...的研究经历了几个发展阶段：

第一阶段（时间段）：奠基期
  - 主要学者和代表性观点
  - 该阶段的总体特征

第二阶段（时间段）：深化期
  - ...

第三阶段（时间段）：转向期
  - ...

示例：

明清之际思想史研究大致经历了三个阶段：1980 年代的「启蒙」叙事、1990 年代的「内在理路」转向，以及 2010 年以来的「全球史」视野...

docs.title: 方式三：按论争焦点
docs.text:
适用于：学界对某个问题有明显分歧

结构：

学界关于...问题存在几种主要观点：

观点 A：...
  - 支持者：...
  - 论据：...

观点 B：...
  - 支持者：...
  - 论据：...

观点 C：...
  - 支持者：...
  - 论据：...

三种观点的分歧核心在于...，尚未达成共识的方面...

示例：

关于晚明思想变革的性质，学界存在三种主要观点：以余英时为代表的「内在理路」说认为...；以沟口雄三为代表的「中国基体」说主张...；近年来有学者提出...

docs.title: 三、文献综述的写作步骤
Step 1：收集与分类
docs.text:
1. 通读每篇文献，做笔记：核心论点、使用的材料、研究方法
  2. 给每篇文献贴标签（可一篇多标签）：
  3. 主题标签：#政治史 #思想史 #文学史
  4. 方法标签：#考证 #阐释 #比较
  5. 立场标签：#支持X #反对Y #补充Z
  6. 按标签归类，形成综述的初步结构

docs.title: Step 2：寻找对话关系
docs.text:
问自己： - 这些学者是在回答同一个问题吗？ - 他们之间有哪些共识？ - 他们在哪些点上争论？ - 谁继承了谁？谁反驳了谁？ - 有没有被忽视的声音？

常用句式： - 「A 的研究开创了...，但其局限在于...」 - 「B 在此基础上推进了...，但仍未解决...」 - 「C 的研究与 A 形成对话，他认为...」 - 「值得注意的是，D 从...角度提出了不同看法」

docs.title: Step 3：定位研究空白
docs.text:
空白类型： - 材料空白：某个重要文本/史料尚未被充分研究 - 视角空白：已有研究都从 X 角度切入，没人从 Y 角度 - 方法空白：学界多用 A 方法，B 方法的潜力未被发掘 - 论题空白：某个子问题一直被忽视

表达研究空白： - 「然而，已有研究尚未充分关注...」 - 「值得注意的是，关于...的讨论仍显不足」 - 「现有研究多聚焦于...，而对...则缺乏深入探讨」 - 「上述研究为本文奠定了基础，但它们共同留下了一个问题：...」

docs.title: Step 4：说明你的位置
docs.text:
在综述末尾，明确说明： - 你的研究如何回应这些文献 - 你站在哪一派/哪条脉络上 - 你的新贡献是什么

句式： - 「基于上述回顾，本文拟从...角度切入，探讨...」 - 「不同于 A 的...观点，本文主张...」 - 「借鉴 B 的...方法，本文将其运用于...」

docs.title: 四、文献综述的常见错误
docs.text: 错误 修正 罗列式：A 说... B 说... C 说... 按主题/脉络组织，呈现对话关系 只述不评：只总结观点，不做评价 每段都要指出贡献、局限或关联 引用过旧：大量引用几十年前的文献 平衡经典文献与前沿研究 忽略相反观点 主动呈现论争，再说明你的立场 综述与研究脱节 每部分都要回扣到你的研究问题 引用二手文献代替一手 尽量引用原始出处

docs.title: 五、字数与比例
docs.text:
• 绪论中的文献综述：硕士 2000-3000 字，博士 3000-5000 字
  • 独立文献综述章节：硕士 5000-8000 字，博士 8000-15000 字
  • 占全文比例：约 15-25%

docs.title: 六、学术诚信
docs.text:
• 综述中的每个观点都要注明出处
  • 概述他人观点时，准确反映原意，不歪曲
  • 区分「直接引用」、「间接引述」、「观点概述」
  • 不编造文献信息，不虚构学者观点
  • 转述时使用自己的语言，避免改写式抄袭

docs.title: 七、进阶技巧
docs.text:
1. 地图意识：把文献综述想象成绘制一幅「学界地图」，标注主要山脉（主流观点）、河流（发展脉络）、空白地带（研究空白）。

2. 漏斗结构：从宽到窄。先综述最宏观的讨论，逐步聚焦到与你的具体议题直接相关的文献。

3. 批判性阅读：不是「他研究了什么」，而是「他为什么这样研究」、「他预设了什么」、「他遗漏了什么」。

4. 反向利用：找到批评某篇文献的后续研究，它们往往指出了最有价值的空白。

docs.title: 论文章节结构与写作要点
一、学位论文标准结构（人文社科）
硕士论文
docs.text:
摘要（中文）
摘要（英文）
目次
圖表目次
緒論
  1.1 研究背景與動機
  1.2 研究問題
  1.3 文獻回顧
  1.4 研究方法
  1.5 章節安排
第 2 章 核心理論/背景
第 3 章 主要論證（一）
第 4 章 主要論證（二）
第 5 章 延伸討論/對話
結論
  總結發現
  研究貢獻
  研究限制
  未來展望
參考文獻

docs.title: 本科毕业论文
docs.text:
摘要
緒論
第 1 章 背景與方法
第 2 章 文本分析/個案研究
第 3 章 討論
結論
參考文獻

docs.title: 緒論（佔全文 8-12%）
docs.text:
研究背景與動機： - 從宏觀問題切入，逐步聚焦到你的具體議題 - 說明這個問題為什麼重要（學術價值 + 現實意義） - 避免「古今中外」式泛泛而談，聚焦核心脈絡

研究問題： - 明確提出 1-3 個具體的研究問題 - 問題要有可回答性，避免過大或過模糊 - 格式示例：「本研究旨在探討...」、「本文關注的核心問題是...」

文獻回顧（緒論版，簡述）： - 概述已有研究的幾條主要線索 - 指出這些研究未能解決的問題（gap） - 你的研究如何填補這個 gap

研究方法： - 具體說明你的研究路徑（文本細讀/歷史考證/比較分析/思想史方法等） - 材料範圍（你分析了哪些文本/使用了哪些史料） - 論證策略（你是如何從材料推導出論點的）

docs.title: 正文章節（佔全文 70-80%）
docs.text:
每章標準結構：

章標題
  開門見山：本章核心論點（1-2 段）
  節 1：背景鋪墊或理論框架
  節 2-3：核心論證（分層推進）
  節 4：小結/過渡到下一章

論證技巧： - 每段一個論點，段首主題句明確 - 論點 → 證據（引文/史料/數據） → 分析 → 小結 - 引文不要堆砌，每條引文後要有你的詮釋 - 轉折處使用過渡句：「然而...」、「值得注意的是...」、「相較之下...」

引文使用原則： - 直接引用：保留原文，加引號，注明出處 - 間接引述：用自己的話概括，仍需注明出處 - 概述觀點：多位學者的共通看法，可合併引用 - 引文長度：一般不要超過 100 字，過長引文單獨成段

docs.title: 結論（佔全文 8-10%）
docs.text:
總結發現： - 逐條回答緒論中提出的研究問題 - 概括各章的核心發現，整合為整體論點

研究貢獻： - 理論層面：推進了什麼認識、修正了什麼觀點 - 方法層面：開闢了什麼新路徑 - 材料層面：發掘了什麼新史料/新文本

研究限制： - 坦誠說明本研究未能解決的問題 - 解釋原因（材料限制/篇幅限制/方法局限） - 避免過度謙虛，但也不要迴避不足

未來展望： - 指出本研究可延伸的方向 - 提示後續研究者可關注的問題

docs.title: 學術中文要點
docs.text:
應該做的： - 使用書面語：「探討」、「梳理」、「揭示」、「指出」 - 邏輯連接清晰：「首先...其次...最後...」、「一方面...另一方面...」 - 適度使用長句，但避免過度歐化 - 術語一致：同一概念全文統一譯名/表述

避免的： - 口語詞：「我覺得」、「其實」、「蠻」、「挺」 - 網路用語：「yyds」、「絕絕子」、「破防」 - 主觀情緒詞：「令人震驚的是」、「不可思議的是」 - 模糊量詞：「很多」、「一些」、「大概」→ 改用具體數據或明確範圍

docs.title: 常用學術表達
docs.text: 場景 推薦表達 提出觀點 本文認為...、筆者主張...、本研究提出... 引述他人 如余英時所言...、據王汎森的研究...、有學者指出... 表示轉折 然而、相對而言、值得注意的是、與此形成對照的是 表示補充 此外、與此同時、不僅如此、進一步而言 表示因果 由此可見、因此、基於此、鑒於... 表示總結 綜上所述、總括而言、歸結起來 表示限定 在某種程度上、就...而言、至少就本文所論

docs.title: 四、常見問題
docs.text:
問題 1：章節之間缺乏銜接 - 對策：每章結尾寫 1-2 段過渡，說明本章發現如何引出下一章的問題

問題 2：引文過多，自己的聲音被淹沒 - 對策：遵循「引文 + 詮釋」原則，每條引文後必須有你自己的分析

問題 3：論點過大，論證撐不住 - 對策：把大論題拆解為 2-3 個可操作的子問題，分章論證

問題 4：文獻回顧像書目羅列 - 對策：按主題/論爭/脈絡組織，每組文獻要說明它們之間的關係

問題 5：結論變成摘要重複 - 對策：結論要「昇華」，把具體發現提升到方法論/理論層面

docs.title: 开题报告/研究计划模板
一、开题报告标准结构
docs.text:
一、研究题目
二、研究背景与动机
三、文献回顾
四、研究问题
五、研究方法
六、章节安排
七、预期贡献
八、研究进度
九、参考文献

docs.title: 一、研究题目
docs.text:
• 准确、具体，避免过大过空
  • 体现核心研究对象和方法视角
  • 可包含副标题，用破折号连接

示例： - 主标题：清初遗民文人的身份认同与书写策略 - 副标题：以顾炎武、黄宗羲为中心的考察

docs.title: 二、研究背景与动机
docs.text:
结构： 1. 宏观背景（1段）：该议题在学术史或现实中的位置 2. 具体契机（1段）：什么具体现象/文本/事件引发你的兴趣 3. 现有不足（1-2段）：已有研究做到了什么、没做到什么 4. 你的切入点（1段）：你打算从什么角度切入

字数：硕士 800-1500 字，博士 1500-2500 字

docs.title: 三、文献回顾
docs.text:
不要做成书目罗列。按以下逻辑组织：

方法一：按主题线索

现有研究主要从三个角度展开：
（一）政治史视角...
（二）思想史视角...
（三）文学史视角...

方法二：按时间脉络

关于本议题的研究大致经历了三个阶段：
第一阶段（1980-2000）：...
第二阶段（2000-2015）：...
第三阶段（2015至今）：...

方法三：按论争焦点

学界关于此问题存在几种主要观点：...
观点A：...
观点B：...
两种观点的分歧在于...

关键任务：在回顾末尾明确指出 research gap（研究空白）

docs.title: 四、研究问题
docs.text:
• 1-3 个核心问题，用问句或陈述句呈现
  • 问题之间要有逻辑关联
  • 每个问题都要能在正文中得到回答

格式：

基于上述文献回顾，本研究拟探讨以下核心问题：

（一）...？
（二）...？
（三）...？

docs.title: 五、研究方法
docs.text:
需要说明： 1. 研究路径：文本细读 / 历史考证 / 比较分析 / 田野调查 / 数字人文等 2. 材料范围：你计划分析哪些文本/史料/数据 3. 论证策略：如何从材料推导结论 4. 理论框架（如有）：使用什么理论视角

示例：

本研究采取思想史与文学史交叉的方法路径。在材料层面，以《明夷待访录》《日知录》为核心文本，辅以顾炎武、黄宗羲的书信、序跋及相关史料。在论证策略上，先梳理清初政治文化语境，再分析两位遗民文人的身份认同危机，最后考察其如何在书写中建构自我形象。

docs.title: 六、章节安排
docs.text:
用提纲形式呈现，每章说明： - 本章解决什么问题 - 主要论点 - 与前后章的关系

格式：

本文预计分五章：

第一章 绪论
  阐述研究背景、问题意识、文献回顾、方法与章节安排。

第二章 清初遗民文人群体的形成
  考察明清易代之际文人的政治选择与身份困境，为后文分析奠定历史语境。

第三章 顾炎武的身份认同与经世书写
  通过细读《日知录》，分析顾炎武如何在学术书写中调和遗民身份与现实关怀。

第四章 黄宗羲的遗民叙事与历史书写
  ...

第五章 结论
  总结两位遗民文人书写策略的异同，讨论清初遗民书写的普遍模式与历史意义。

docs.title: 七、预期贡献
docs.text:
• 学术贡献：填补了什么空白、修正了什么观点
  • 方法贡献：尝试了哪些新的分析路径
  • 现实意义（如适用）：对当下的启示

注意：避免过度夸大，保持学术谦逊

docs.title: 九、参考文献
docs.text:
• 列出开题报告中引用的所有文献
  • 按学术规范格式排列（中文在前，外文在后）
  • 数量参考：硕士 30-50 条，博士 50-80 条

docs.title: 三、常见错误
docs.text: 错误 修正 题目过大：「中国古代文学研究」 缩小范围：「清初遗民文人的身份认同——以顾炎武为中心」 文献回顾像书单 按主题/脉络组织，说明文献间关系 研究问题太泛 确保每个问题都能在正文中得到明确回答 方法描述空洞：「采用文本分析法」 具体说明：分析哪些文本、关注什么层面、如何操作 进度安排不切实际 留出修改和意外延误的时间 贡献夸大 具体说明填补了什么小空白，而非「填补学界空白」

docs.title: 四、自检清单
docs.text: 提交前确认： - [ ] 题目具体、可操作 - [ ] 文献回顾有逻辑线索，不是罗列 - [ ] 明确指出了研究空白 - [ ] 研究问题 1-3 个，且互不重复 - [ ] 方法描述足够具体 - [ ] 章节安排每章都有明确任务 - [ ] 预期贡献务实，不夸大 - [ ] 进度安排留有余地 - [ ] 参考文献格式统一 - [ ] 全文无错别字

docs.title: Image Generation - AI Image Creation Powered by CellCog
docs.text: Create professional images with AI - from single images to consistent character sets to product photography.

docs.title: How to Use
docs.text:
For your first CellCog task in a session, read the cellcog skill for the full SDK reference — file handling, chat modes, timeouts, and more.

OpenClaw (fire-and-forget):

result = client.create_chat(
    prompt="[your task prompt]",
    notify_session_key="agent:main:main",
    task_label="my-task",
    chat_mode="agent",
)

All agents except OpenClaw (blocks until done):

from cellcog import CellCogClient
client = CellCogClient(agent_provider="openclaw|cursor|claude-code|codex|...")
result = client.create_chat(
    prompt="[your task prompt]",
    task_label="my-task",
    chat_mode="agent",
)
print(result["message"])

docs.title: What Models Do We Use
docs.text:
Model Provider Primary Use Nano Banana 2 (Gemini 3.1 Flash Image) Google Default image generation — photorealistic scenes, complex compositions, text rendering, multi-turn character consistency GPT Image 1.5 OpenAI Transparent background images — logos, stickers, product cutouts, overlay graphics Recraft Recraft AI Scalable vector illustrations (SVG) and icon generation

Nano Banana 2 is the default model for all image generation. CellCog's agents intelligently route to other models when the task calls for it — for example, transparent PNGs are automatically handled by GPT Image 1.5, and vector/icon requests go to Recraft. If you'd prefer a specific model, just mention it in your prompt (e.g., "use ChatGPT/OpenAI image generation").

docs.title: Single Image Creation
docs.text:
Generate any image from a text description:

  • Scenes: "A cozy coffee shop interior with morning light streaming through windows"
  • Portraits: "Professional headshot of a confident woman in business attire"
  • Products: "Minimalist product shot of a white sneaker on a marble surface"
  • Abstract: "Geometric abstract art in navy and gold"
  • Nature: "Misty mountain landscape at sunrise with a lone hiker"

docs.title: Image Editing
docs.text:
Transform existing images:

  • Style Transfer: "Transform this photo into a watercolor painting"
  • Background Removal: "Remove the background and place on a clean white backdrop"
  • Enhancement: "Enhance the colors and add dramatic lighting"
  • Modification: "Change the person's outfit to a red dress"

docs.title: Consistent Characters
docs.text:
Create multiple images of the same character in different scenarios:

  • Character Series: "Create a tech entrepreneur character, then show them: 1) At their desk coding, 2) Presenting to investors, 3) Celebrating a product launch"
  • Mascot Variations: "Design a friendly robot mascot, then create versions for: welcome page, error page, success message, loading screen"
  • Story Sequences: "Create a main character, then illustrate them in 5 scenes of a journey"

This is powerful for: - Comic strips and storyboards - Marketing campaigns with consistent characters - Video frame generation - Brand mascots across contexts

docs.title: Product Photography Style
docs.text:
Professional product visuals:

  • Hero Shots: "Product hero shot of a smartwatch on a gradient background"
  • Lifestyle Shots: "Smartphone being used by a person in a modern living room"
  • Flat Lays: "Flat lay of skincare products with botanical elements"
  • 360 Views: "Multiple angles of a leather handbag - front, side, back, detail"

docs.title: Sets of Related Images
docs.text:
Multiple cohesive images for campaigns or collections:

  • Social Media Sets: "5 Instagram post images for a fitness brand - consistent style, varied content"
  • Website Heroes: "3 hero images for a SaaS landing page - professional, modern, tech-focused"
  • Ad Variations: "4 versions of a product ad with different backgrounds and moods"
  • Blog Illustrations: "Set of 6 illustrations for a blog post about productivity tips"

docs.title: Reference-Based Generation
docs.text:
Use existing images as references for style, character, or composition:

  • Style Matching: "Create a new image in the same artistic style as this reference"
  • Character Consistency: "Using this person as reference, create a new scene with them hiking"
  • Brand Alignment: "Create product images matching this brand's visual style"
  • Composition Reference: "Create a similar composition but with different subjects"

docs.title: Image Specifications
docs.text:
Aspect Options Aspect Ratios 1:1 (square), 16:9, 9:16, 4:3, 3:4, 3:2, 2:3, 21:9 Sizes 1K (~1024px), 2K (~2048px), 4K (~4096px) Styles Photorealistic, illustration, watercolor, oil painting, anime, digital art, vector Formats PNG (default)

Size recommendations: - 1K: Quick iterations, thumbnails, social media posts, drafts - 2K: Standard web content, presentations, marketing materials - 4K: Hero images, print materials, final deliverables where detail matters

docs.title: When to Use Agent Team Mode
docs.text:
For image generation, chat_mode="agent team" is recommended for: - Complex scenes requiring multiple elements - Consistent character series - Reference-based generation requiring analysis - Sets of related images

For simple single images, chat_mode="agent" can work faster.

docs.title: Example Image Prompts
docs.text:
Professional headshot:

"Create a professional headshot of a friendly Asian woman in her 30s, wearing a navy blazer, soft studio lighting, neutral gray background, confident but approachable expression. 1:1 square, 2K quality, photorealistic."

Product photography:

"Product shot of a premium wireless earbuds case, matte black finish, on a reflective dark surface with subtle blue accent lighting. Minimalist, high-end tech aesthetic. 4:3 landscape, 4K for hero image."

Consistent character set:

"Create a character: young Black male software developer, casual style with glasses, friendly demeanor. Then create 4 images: 1. Working at a standing desk with multiple monitors 2. In a video call meeting, explaining something 3. At a coffee shop with laptop, thinking 4. Celebrating with team, high-fiving Keep the character exactly consistent across all images."

Social media set:

"Create 5 Instagram posts for a plant-based meal delivery service: 1. Colorful Buddha bowl from above 2. Happy person unpacking delivery 3. Meal prep containers arranged neatly 4. Close-up of fresh ingredients 5. Before/after showing ingredients to finished dish Style: bright, fresh, appetizing, consistent warm color grading. 1:1 square format."

Style transfer:

"Transform this uploaded photo of a city street into a Studio Ghibli anime style illustration. Keep the composition and elements but apply the characteristic Ghibli warmth, soft clouds, and whimsical details."

docs.title: Tips for Better Images
docs.text:
1. Be descriptive: "Woman in office" is vague. "Confident woman in her 40s, silver blazer, modern glass-walled office, warm afternoon light" is better.

  2. Specify style: "Photorealistic", "digital illustration", "watercolor", "minimalist vector".

  3. Describe lighting: "Soft natural light", "dramatic side lighting", "golden hour glow", "studio lighting".

  4. Include mood: "Professional and confident", "warm and inviting", "energetic and vibrant".

  5. Mention composition: "Rule of thirds", "centered symmetry", "close-up", "wide establishing shot".

  6. For consistency: When creating character series, describe the character in detail first, then reference "the same character" in subsequent prompts.

docs.title: Integration
docs.text:
This skill is designed to work within the broader music generation research workflow:

  1. Input: Papers that have passed quality filtering
  2. Processing: Applies appropriate SOP template based on topic classification

docs.title: Usage in Research Workflow
docs.text:
When processing papers from arXiv search results:

# Example workflow integration
for paper in filtered_papers:
    topic = classify_paper(paper)  # method, dataset, multimodal, etc.
    summary = paper_summarize(
        title=paper.title,
        authors=paper.authors, 
        abstract=paper.abstract,
        topic=topic,

docs.title: Paper Summarize Skill
docs.text: This skill provides academic-grade paper summarization with dynamic Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) selection based on paper topic classification.

docs.title: Capabilities

  • Rigorous Analysis: Follows top-tier conference review criteria (NeurIPS/ICML/ICLR/ACL)

  • dataset: Dataset/benchmark papers

docs.title: Quality Standards
docs.text:

  • Experimental Assessment: 1000+ characters, rigorous evaluation with explicit focus on datasets used for training and testing, protocol rigor, baseline fairness, ablation completeness, and statistical significance
  • Overall Analysis: 3000+ characters, critical perspective
  • Technical Precision: Correct terminology, specific method names, exact metrics

  1. Paper Discovery: Works with arXiv search results

    topic: "dataset",

    abstract: "We introduce MusicSem, a semantically rich language-audio dataset..."
  },
  {
    title: "Art2Mus: Artwork-to-Music Generation via Visual Conditioning",
    topic: "multimodal",
    authors: "Ivan Rinaldi, Matteo Mendula, Nicola Fanelli, et al.",
    abstract: "Art2Mus enables artwork-to-music generation through visual conditioning..."
  }
];

docs.title: Step 2: Apply Appropriate SOP Template
docs.text:
// For each paper, select SOP based on topic
function getPaperSummary(paper) {
  const { title, authors, abstract, topic } = paper;

  // Load appropriate SOP template
  const sopTemplate = getSOPForTopic(topic);

  // Fill template variables
  const userPrompt = sopTemplate
    .replace('{{title}}', title)
    .replace('{{authors}}', authors)
    .replace('{{abstract}}', abstract)
    .replace('{{topic}}', topic);

  // Combine with system prompt
  const fullPrompt = SYSTEM_PROMPT + '\n\n' + userPrompt;

  return fullPrompt;
}

docs.title: Step 3: Generate and Save Summary
docs.text:
// Generate summary using AI model
const summary = generateSummary(fullPrompt);

// Save to organized directory structure
const safeTitle = title.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9]/g, '_');
const filePath = `research/music_generation/ai_summaries/${safeTitle}.md`;
writeFile(filePath, summary);

// Save prompt for reproducibility
const promptPath = `research/music_generation/prompts/${safeTitle}_prompt.txt`;
writeFile(promptPath, fullPrompt);

docs.text:
All notable changes to this skill are documented here, including anything an agent or user must do when upgrading. Format follows Keep a Changelog; versions follow SemVer and match version in SKILL.md frontmatter.

Read this before upgrading. General upgrade rules:

  • OpenClaw hook changes only take effect after re-copying and restarting. The hook runs from a copy: re-run cp -r ~/.openclaw/skills/self-improving-agent/hooks/openclaw ~/.openclaw/hooks/self-improvement and restart the gateway after upgrading.
  • .learnings/ files are user data and are never migrated or overwritten by upgrades; first-use initialisation is idempotent and only creates missing files.

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • GitHub Actions CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml at the repo root): runs the hook test suite, type-checks handler.ts (strict mode, against a CI-only type stub), and syntax-checks extract-skill.sh on every push to master and every PR.

Install by copying the subfolder, not the repo root — install/upgrade commands in the docs are updated.
  • SKILL.md frontmatter name corrected from self-improvement to self-improving-agent to match the skill folder name, as the Agent Skills spec requires. The OpenClaw hook keeps its self-improvement name, so existing hook installs and openclaw hooks enable self-improvement are unaffected.

  2. Nothing changes for OpenClaw installs beyond the usual re-copy of the hook directory; .learnings/ data and entry formats are unaffected.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Pattern-Key generalized to all three log files: the ERRORS.md and FEATURE_REQUESTS.md entry formats now carry a Pattern-Key field (recommended for errors, optional for features), joining LEARNINGS.md where it was previously limited to the simplify-and-harden feed.
  • Pattern-Key Taxonomy section in SKILL.md: controlled area.symptom namespaces (api, auth, build, config, deps, fs, net, runtime, shell, vcs, plus simplify/harden), with reuse-before-mint and one-key-per-entry rules.
  • The OpenClaw session-end error sweep stamps deterministic Pattern-Key values on auto-detected entries (e.g. ModuleNotFoundError → deps.module-not-found), making them recurrence-countable with no agent discipline required.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Grep-by-Pattern-Key is now the documented default dedup step when logging; keyword grep is the fallback. Recurrences are folded into the existing entry (Recurrence-Count, Last-Seen, See Also) instead of duplicated.
  • Tightened SKILL.md (hook sections, taxonomy, duplicated setup blocks) to keep the always-loaded skill prompt compact.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • scripts/extract-skill.sh is now committed with the executable bit set — previously every install needed a manual chmod +x.

docs.title: Upgrade notes (0.2.0 → 0.3.0)
docs.text:
1. Re-copy the OpenClaw hook and restart the gateway (see general rules above) to get Pattern-Key stamping on swept entries.
  2. Existing .learnings/ entries without Pattern-Key remain valid — the field is additive. Add keys opportunistically when touching old entries.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• OpenClaw session-end error sweep (hooks/openclaw/): the hook now also fires on command:new / command:reset, scans the ended session's transcript for the same error patterns as scripts/error-detector.sh, and appends pending entries (Source: openclaw-error-sweep) to <workspace>/.learnings/ERRORS.md. Opt-in: runs only when <workspace>/.learnings/ exists. Excerpts are capped, truncated, redacted, and deduplicated.
  • Pending-triage note in the bootstrap reminder when auto-detected error entries await review.
  • Test suite: node --test hooks/openclaw/handler.test.js (no dependencies).
  • Docs: "Error Detection on OpenClaw" section and platform support matrix in references/openclaw-integration.md; uninstall guide in references/uninstall.md; this changelog.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• hooks/openclaw/HOOK.md events metadata is now ["agent:bootstrap", "command:new", "command:reset"].
  • Docs now state explicitly that scripts/error-detector.sh is Claude Code only (OpenClaw has no PostToolUse equivalent).

docs.title: Upgrade notes (0.1.x → 0.2.0)
docs.text:
1. Re-copy the hook and restart the gateway (see general rules above).
  2. To enable the new error sweep: mkdir -p ~/.openclaw/workspace/.learnings. Without that directory, behavior is identical to 0.1.0.
  3. No breaking changes; no .learnings/ migration needed.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Initial release: SKILL.md with logging formats (LEARNINGS.md, ERRORS.md, FEATURE_REQUESTS.md), promotion workflow, and skill extraction.
  • OpenClaw bootstrap-reminder hook (agent:bootstrap).
  • Claude Code hook scripts: activator.sh (UserPromptSubmit) and error-detector.sh (PostToolUse).

docs.title: Self-Improvement Skill
docs.text: Log learnings and errors to markdown files for continuous improvement. Agents can later process these into fixes, and important learnings get promoted to workspace memory. This version of the skill is built for OpenClaw only — for other agents, see the original multi-agent version at https://github.com/pskoett/pskoett-ai-skills.

docs.title: First-Use Initialisation
docs.text:
Before logging anything, ensure the .learnings/ directory and files exist in the project or workspace root. If any are missing, create them:

mkdir -p .learnings
[ -f .learnings/LEARNINGS.md ] || printf "# Learnings

Corrections, insights, and knowledge gaps captured during development.

**Categories**: correction | insight | knowledge_gap | best_practice

---
" > .learnings/LEARNINGS.md
[ -f .learnings/ERRORS.md ] || printf "# Errors

Command failures and integration errors.

---
" > .learnings/ERRORS.md
[ -f .learnings/FEATURE_REQUESTS.md ] || printf "# Feature Requests

Capabilities requested by the user.

---
" > .learnings/FEATURE_REQUESTS.md

Never overwrite existing files. This is a no-op if .learnings/ is already initialised.

Do not log secrets, tokens, private keys, environment variables, or full source/config files unless the user explicitly asks for that level of detail. Prefer short summaries or redacted excerpts over raw command output or full transcripts.

If you want automatic reminders and session-end error detection, enable the opt-in hook described in Optional: Enable Hook.

docs.title: Quick Reference
docs.text: Situation Action Command/operation fails Log to .learnings/ERRORS.md User corrects you Log to .learnings/LEARNINGS.md with category correction User wants missing feature Log to .learnings/FEATURE_REQUESTS.md API/external tool fails Log to .learnings/ERRORS.md with integration details Knowledge was outdated Log to .learnings/LEARNINGS.md with category knowledge_gap Found better approach Log to .learnings/LEARNINGS.md with category best_practice Simplify/Harden recurring patterns Log/update .learnings/LEARNINGS.md with Source: simplify-and-harden and a stable Pattern-Key Similar to existing entry Grep by Pattern-Key first, link with **See Also**, bump Recurrence-Count Workflow improvements Promote to AGENTS.md (workspace) Tool gotchas Promote to TOOLS.md (workspace) Behavioral patterns Promote to SOUL.md (workspace)

docs.title: OpenClaw Setup
docs.text: OpenClaw uses workspace-based prompt injection with automatic skill loading.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Via ClawdHub (recommended):

clawdhub install self-improving-agent

Manual (the skill lives in the repo's self-improving-agent/ subfolder; copy that folder, not the repo root):

git clone https://github.com/peterskoett/self-improving-agent.git /tmp/self-improving-agent-repo
cp -r /tmp/self-improving-agent-repo/self-improving-agent ~/.openclaw/skills/self-improving-agent

Remade for openclaw from original repo : https://github.com/pskoett/pskoett-ai-skills - https://github.com/pskoett/pskoett-ai-skills/tree/main/skills/self-improvement

docs.title: Workspace Structure
docs.text:
OpenClaw injects these files into every session:

~/.openclaw/workspace/
├── AGENTS.md          # Multi-agent workflows, delegation patterns
├── SOUL.md            # Behavioral guidelines, personality, principles
├── TOOLS.md           # Tool capabilities, integration gotchas
├── MEMORY.md          # Long-term memory (main session only)
├── memory/            # Daily memory files
│   └── YYYY-MM-DD.md
└── .learnings/        # This skill's log files
    ├── LEARNINGS.md
    ├── ERRORS.md
    └── FEATURE_REQUESTS.md

docs.title: Create Learning Files
docs.text:
mkdir -p ~/.openclaw/workspace/.learnings

Then create the log files (or copy from assets/): - LEARNINGS.md — corrections, knowledge gaps, best practices - ERRORS.md — command failures, exceptions - FEATURE_REQUESTS.md — user-requested capabilities

docs.title: Promotion Targets
docs.text:
When learnings prove broadly applicable, promote them to workspace files:

Learning Type Promote To Example Behavioral patterns SOUL.md "Be concise, avoid disclaimers" Workflow improvements AGENTS.md "Spawn sub-agents for long tasks" Tool gotchas TOOLS.md "Git push needs auth configured first"

docs.title: Inter-Session Communication
docs.text:
OpenClaw provides tools to share learnings across sessions:

  • sessions_list — View active/recent sessions
  • sessions_history — Read another session's transcript
  • sessions_send — Send a learning to another session
  • sessions_spawn — Spawn a sub-agent for background work

Use these only in trusted environments and only when the user explicitly wants cross-session sharing. Prefer sending a short sanitized summary and relevant file paths, not raw transcripts, secrets, or full command output.

docs.title: Optional: Enable Hook
docs.text:
For automatic reminders at session start and error detection at session end:

cp -r ~/.openclaw/skills/self-improving-agent/hooks/openclaw ~/.openclaw/hooks/self-improvement
openclaw hooks enable self-improvement

Fires on agent:bootstrap (injects the reminder, plus a pending-triage note when auto-detected errors await review) and on command:new/command:reset (sweeps the ended session's transcript for error patterns into <workspace>/.learnings/ERRORS.md; opt-in — runs only when .learnings/ exists). OpenClaw has no per-tool-call hook event, so error detection happens at session end. See references/openclaw-integration.md for details and sweep limitations.

docs.title: Learning Entry
docs.text:
Append to .learnings/LEARNINGS.md:

## [LRN-YYYYMMDD-XXX] category

**Logged**: ISO-8601 timestamp
**Priority**: low | medium | high | critical
**Status**: pending
**Area**: frontend | backend | infra | tests | docs | config

### Summary
One-line description of what was learned

### Details
Full context: what happened, what was wrong, what's correct

### Suggested Action
Specific fix or improvement to make

### Metadata
- Source: conversation | error | user_feedback
- Related Files: path/to/file.ext
- Tags: tag1, tag2
- See Also: LRN-20250110-001 (if related to existing entry)
- Pattern-Key: area.symptom (recommended; e.g. deps.module-not-found, simplify.dead_code — see Pattern-Key Taxonomy)
- Recurrence-Count: 1 (optional)
- First-Seen: 2025-01-15 (optional)
- Last-Seen: 2025-01-15 (optional)

---

docs.title: Error Entry
docs.text:
Append to .learnings/ERRORS.md:

## [ERR-YYYYMMDD-XXX] skill_or_command_name

**Logged**: ISO-8601 timestamp
**Priority**: high
**Status**: pending
**Area**: frontend | backend | infra | tests | docs | config

### Summary
Brief description of what failed

### Error

Actual error message or output

### Context
- Command/operation attempted
- Input or parameters used
- Environment details if relevant
- Summary or redacted excerpt of relevant output (avoid full transcripts and secret-bearing data by default)

### Suggested Fix
If identifiable, what might resolve this

### Metadata
- Reproducible: yes | no | unknown
- Related Files: path/to/file.ext
- See Also: ERR-20250110-001 (if recurring)
- Pattern-Key: area.symptom (recommended; e.g. net.connection-refused — see Pattern-Key Taxonomy)
- Recurrence-Count: 1 (optional)
- First-Seen: 2025-01-15 (optional)
- Last-Seen: 2025-01-15 (optional)

---

docs.title: Feature Request Entry
docs.text:
Append to .learnings/FEATURE_REQUESTS.md:

## [FEAT-YYYYMMDD-XXX] capability_name

**Logged**: ISO-8601 timestamp
**Priority**: medium
**Status**: pending
**Area**: frontend | backend | infra | tests | docs | config

### Requested Capability
What the user wanted to do

### User Context
Why they needed it, what problem they're solving

### Complexity Estimate
simple | medium | complex

### Suggested Implementation
How this could be built, what it might extend

### Metadata
- Frequency: first_time | recurring
- Related Features: existing_feature_name
- Pattern-Key: area.symptom (optional — features usually dedupe by capability name; use a key only for recurring themes, e.g. api.missing-endpoint)

---

docs.title: ID Generation
docs.text:
Format: TYPE-YYYYMMDD-XXX - TYPE: LRN (learning), ERR (error), FEAT (feature) - YYYYMMDD: Current date - XXX: Sequential number or random 3 chars (e.g., 001, A7B)

Examples: LRN-20250115-001, ERR-20250115-A3F, FEAT-20250115-002

docs.title: Resolving Entries
docs.text:
When an issue is fixed, update the entry:

  1. Change **Status**: pending → **Status**: resolved
  2. Add resolution block after Metadata:
### Resolution
- **Resolved**: 2025-01-16T09:00:00Z
- **Commit/PR**: abc123 or #42
- **Notes**: Brief description of what was done

Other status values: - in_progress - Actively being worked on - wont_fix - Decided not to address (add reason in Resolution notes) - promoted - Elevated to a workspace file (SOUL.md, TOOLS.md, AGENTS.md)

docs.title: Promoting to Workspace Memory
docs.text: When a learning is broadly applicable (not a one-off fix), promote it to a workspace file so every session inherits it.

docs.title: When to Promote
docs.text:
• Learning applies across multiple files/features
  • Knowledge any contributor (human or AI) should know
  • Prevents recurring mistakes
  • Documents project-specific conventions

docs.title: Promotion Targets
docs.text:
Target What Belongs There SOUL.md Behavioral guidelines, communication style, principles TOOLS.md Tool capabilities, usage patterns, integration gotchas AGENTS.md Workflows, delegation patterns, automation rules

When the learning is specific to a project repo you work in (not the workspace), promote to that project's own agent file (e.g. its AGENTS.md) instead.

docs.title: How to Promote
docs.text:
1. Distill the learning into a concise rule or fact
  2. Add to appropriate section in target file (create file if needed)
  3. Update original entry:
  4. Change **Status**: pending → **Status**: promoted
  5. Add **Promoted**: SOUL.md, TOOLS.md, or AGENTS.md

docs.title: Promotion Examples
docs.text:
Learning (verbose):

Project uses pnpm workspaces. Attempted npm install but failed. Lock file is pnpm-lock.yaml. Must use pnpm install.

In TOOLS.md (concise):

## Build & Dependencies
- Package manager: pnpm (not npm) - use `pnpm install`

Learning (verbose):

When modifying API endpoints, must regenerate TypeScript client. Forgetting this causes type mismatches at runtime.

In AGENTS.md (actionable):

## After API Changes
1. Regenerate client: `pnpm run generate:api`
2. Check for type errors: `pnpm tsc --noEmit`

docs.title: Pattern-Key Taxonomy
docs.text:
Pattern-Key is the stable dedup and recurrence key for entries in all three log files: keyword grep misses semantically identical but differently-worded entries, a shared key does not — and reliable keys are what make Recurrence-Count and the promotion rule work.

Format: area.symptom — exactly two levels, lowercase, hyphenated (e.g. deps.module-not-found). Keep symptoms generic enough to recur: no file names, versions, or hostnames in keys.

Area Scope Example Keys api External API/service behavior api.rate-limit, api.schema-mismatch, api.missing-endpoint auth Credentials, tokens, scopes auth.token-expired, auth.missing-scope build Compilation, bundling, CI build.type-error, build.missing-artifact config Config files, env vars, settings config.missing-env, config.invalid-json deps Package managers, dependencies deps.module-not-found, deps.npm-error, deps.version-conflict fs Filesystem fs.no-such-file, fs.permission-denied net Network connectivity net.connection-refused, net.timeout runtime Language/runtime errors not covered above runtime.type-error, runtime.python-exception shell Shell/CLI mechanics shell.command-not-found, shell.nonzero-exit vcs Git and other version control vcs.fatal-error, vcs.merge-conflict simplify / harden Code-quality patterns from the simplify-and-harden feed simplify.dead_code, harden.input_validation

Rules:

  1. Reuse before minting: grep -rh "Pattern-Key:" .learnings/ | sort -u — a near-match beats a new key.
  2. One key per manual entry; auto-swept OpenClaw entries may carry several — reduce to one when triaging.
  3. Mint new areas sparingly — only when several entries would share one.
  4. Generic sweep keys (runtime.error, runtime.failure) mean "unclassified" — replace with a specific key during triage.

docs.title: Recurring Pattern Detection
docs.text:
If logging something similar to an existing entry:

  1. Search by key first: grep -n "Pattern-Key: area.symptom" .learnings/*.md — this is the default dedup check and catches rewordings that keyword search misses
  2. Fallback keyword search: grep -ri "keyword" .learnings/ for entries logged without a key
  3. Fold, don't duplicate: on a hit, update the existing entry — bump Recurrence-Count, set Last-Seen, add **See Also** — instead of creating a new one
  4. Bump priority if issue keeps recurring
  5. Consider systemic fix: Recurring issues often indicate:
  6. Missing knowledge (→ promote to TOOLS.md or SOUL.md)
  7. Missing automation (→ add to AGENTS.md)
  8. Architectural problem (→ create tech debt ticket)

docs.title: Simplify & Harden Feed
docs.text: Use this workflow to ingest recurring patterns from the simplify-and-harden skill and turn them into durable prompt guidance.

docs.title: Ingestion Workflow
docs.text:
1. Read simplify_and_harden.learning_loop.candidates from the task summary.
  2. For each candidate, use pattern_key as the stable dedupe key.
  3. Search .learnings/LEARNINGS.md for an existing entry with that key:
  4. grep -n "Pattern-Key: <pattern_key>" .learnings/LEARNINGS.md
  5. If found:
  6. Increment Recurrence-Count
  7. Update Last-Seen
  8. Add See Also links to related entries/tasks
  9. If not found:
  10. Create a new LRN-... entry
  11. Set Source: simplify-and-harden
  12. Set Pattern-Key, Recurrence-Count: 1, and First-Seen/Last-Seen

docs.title: Promotion Rule (System Prompt Feedback)
docs.text:
Promote recurring patterns into agent context/system prompt files when all are true:

  • Recurrence-Count >= 3
  • Seen across at least 2 distinct tasks
  • Occurred within a 30-day window

Promotion targets: SOUL.md, TOOLS.md, or AGENTS.md (workspace), or the project's own agent file when the pattern is project-specific.

Write promoted rules as short prevention rules (what to do before/while coding), not long incident write-ups.

docs.title: Periodic Review
docs.text: Review .learnings/ at natural breakpoints:

docs.title: When to Review
docs.text:
• Before starting a new major task
  • After completing a feature
  • When working in an area with past learnings
  • Weekly during active development

docs.title: Quick Status Check
docs.text:
# Count pending items
grep -h "Status\*\*: pending" .learnings/*.md | wc -l

# List pending high-priority items
grep -B5 "Priority\*\*: high" .learnings/*.md | grep "^## \["

# Find learnings for a specific area
grep -l "Area\*\*: backend" .learnings/*.md

docs.title: Review Actions
docs.text:
• Resolve fixed items
  • Promote applicable learnings
  • Link related entries
  • Escalate recurring issues

docs.title: Detection Triggers
docs.text:
Automatically log when you notice:

Corrections (→ learning with correction category): - "No, that's not right..." - "Actually, it should be..." - "You're wrong about..." - "That's outdated..."

Feature Requests (→ feature request): - "Can you also..." - "I wish you could..." - "Is there a way to..." - "Why can't you..."

Knowledge Gaps (→ learning with knowledge_gap category): - User provides information you didn't know - Documentation you referenced is outdated - API behavior differs from your understanding

Errors (→ error entry): - Command returns non-zero exit code - Exception or stack trace - Unexpected output or behavior - Timeout or connection failure

docs.title: Priority Guidelines
docs.text: Priority When to Use critical Blocks core functionality, data loss risk, security issue high Significant impact, affects common workflows, recurring issue medium Moderate impact, workaround exists low Minor inconvenience, edge case, nice-to-have

docs.title: Area Tags
docs.text:
Use to filter learnings by codebase region:

Area Scope frontend UI, components, client-side code backend API, services, server-side code infra CI/CD, deployment, Docker, cloud tests Test files, testing utilities, coverage docs Documentation, comments, READMEs config Configuration files, environment, settings

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Log immediately - context is freshest right after the issue
  2. Be specific - future agents need to understand quickly
  3. Include reproduction steps - especially for errors
  4. Link related files - makes fixes easier
  5. Suggest concrete fixes - not just "investigate"
  6. Use consistent categories - enables filtering
  7. Promote aggressively - if in doubt, add to TOOLS.md or SOUL.md
  8. Review regularly - stale learnings lose value

docs.title: Gitignore Options
docs.text:
Keep learnings local (per-developer):

.learnings/

This repo uses that default to avoid committing sensitive or noisy local logs by accident.

Track learnings in repo (team-wide): Don't add to .gitignore - learnings become shared knowledge.

Hybrid (track templates, ignore entries):

.learnings/*.md
!.learnings/.gitkeep

docs.title: Upgrading & Uninstalling
docs.text: Read CHANGELOG.md before upgrading — it carries per-version notes, and hook changes require re-copying the hook and restarting the gateway. To disable or remove the skill, follow references/uninstall.md: .learnings/ is user data (review before deleting), and content promoted to SOUL.md/TOOLS.md/AGENTS.md stays until removed manually.

docs.title: Automatic Skill Extraction
docs.text: When a learning is valuable enough to become a reusable skill, extract it using the provided helper.

docs.title: Skill Extraction Criteria
docs.text:
A learning qualifies for skill extraction when ANY of these apply:

Criterion Description Recurring Has See Also links to 2+ similar issues Verified Status is resolved with working fix Non-obvious Required actual debugging/investigation to discover Broadly applicable Not project-specific; useful across codebases User-flagged User says "save this as a skill" or similar

docs.title: Extraction Workflow
docs.text:
1. Identify candidate: Learning meets extraction criteria
  2. Run helper (or create manually): bash ~/.openclaw/skills/self-improving-agent/scripts/extract-skill.sh skill-name --dry-run ~/.openclaw/skills/self-improving-agent/scripts/extract-skill.sh skill-name
  3. Customize SKILL.md: Fill in template with learning content
  4. Update learning: Set status to promoted_to_skill, add Skill-Path
  5. Verify: Read skill in fresh session to ensure it's self-contained

docs.title: Manual Extraction
docs.text:
If you prefer manual creation:

  1. Create skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md
  2. Use template from assets/SKILL-TEMPLATE.md
  3. Follow Agent Skills spec:
  4. YAML frontmatter with name and description
  5. Name must match folder name
  6. No README.md inside skill folder

docs.title: Extraction Detection Triggers
docs.text:
Watch for these signals that a learning should become a skill:

In conversation: - "Save this as a skill" - "I keep running into this" - "This would be useful for other projects" - "Remember this pattern"

In learning entries: - Multiple See Also links (recurring issue) - High priority + resolved status - Category: best_practice with broad applicability - User feedback praising the solution

docs.title: Skill Quality Gates
docs.text:
Before extraction, verify:

  • [ ] Solution is tested and working
  • [ ] Description is clear without original context
  • [ ] Code examples are self-contained
  • [ ] No project-specific hardcoded values
  • [ ] Follows skill naming conventions (lowercase, hyphens)

docs.title: Description:
docs.text:
Captures learnings, errors, and corrections to enable continuous improvement for the agent.

This skill is ready for commercial/non-commercial use.

docs.title: Publisher:
docs.text: pskoett

docs.title: License/Terms of Use:
docs.text: MIT-0

docs.title: Use Case:
docs.text: Developers and agent users use this skill to capture corrections, command failures, feature requests, and reusable workflow lessons in local learning files. OpenClaw users can optionally enable a hook that injects reminders and scans ended sessions for error snippets to triage later.

docs.title: Deployment Geography for Use:
docs.text: Global

docs.title: Known Risks and Mitigations:
docs.text: Risk: Persistent local learning files may contain sensitive project context if users or agents log too much detail. Mitigation: Keep .learnings out of version control, review entries before sharing workspaces, and record short redacted summaries rather than secrets, raw transcripts, or full command output. Risk: The optional OpenClaw hook can scan ended session transcripts for error snippets. Mitigation: Enable the hook only in trusted workspaces, avoid it for sessions containing credentials or customer data, and rely on its opt-in .learnings directory behavior to disable scanning when needed.

Categories: correction | insight | knowledge_gap | best_practice Areas: frontend | backend | infra | tests | docs | config Statuses: pending | in_progress | resolved | wont_fix | promoted | promoted_to_skill

docs.title: Status Definitions
docs.text: Status Meaning pending Not yet addressed in_progress Actively being worked on resolved Issue fixed or knowledge integrated wont_fix Decided not to address (reason in Resolution) promoted Elevated to SOUL.md, TOOLS.md, or AGENTS.md promoted_to_skill Extracted as a reusable skill

docs.title: Skill Extraction Fields
docs.text:
When a learning is promoted to a skill, add these fields:

**Status**: promoted_to_skill
**Skill-Path**: skills/skill-name

Example:

## [LRN-20250115-001] best_practice

**Logged**: 2025-01-15T10:00:00Z
**Priority**: high
**Status**: promoted_to_skill
**Skill-Path**: skills/docker-m1-fixes
**Area**: infra

### Summary
Docker build fails on Apple Silicon due to platform mismatch
...

docs.title: Skill Template
docs.text: Template for creating skills extracted from learnings. Copy and customize.

docs.title: SKILL.md Template
docs.text:
---
name: skill-name-here
description: "Concise description of when and why to use this skill. Include trigger conditions."
---

# Skill Name

Brief introduction explaining the problem this skill solves and its origin.

## Quick Reference

| Situation | Action |
|-----------|--------|
| [Trigger 1] | [Action 1] |
| [Trigger 2] | [Action 2] |

## Background

Why this knowledge matters. What problems it prevents. Context from the original learning.

## Solution

### Step-by-Step

1. First step with code or command
2. Second step
3. Verification step

### Code Example

\`\`\`language
// Example code demonstrating the solution
\`\`\`

## Common Variations

- **Variation A**: Description and how to handle
- **Variation B**: Description and how to handle

## Gotchas

- Warning or common mistake #1
- Warning or common mistake #2

## Related

- Link to related documentation
- Link to related skill

## Source

Extracted from learning entry.
- **Learning ID**: LRN-YYYYMMDD-XXX
- **Original Category**: correction | insight | knowledge_gap | best_practice
- **Extraction Date**: YYYY-MM-DD

docs.title: Minimal Template
docs.text:
For simple skills that don't need all sections:

---
name: skill-name-here
description: "What this skill does and when to use it."

docs.title: Self-Improvement Hook
docs.text:
Injects a reminder to evaluate learnings during agent bootstrap, and detects errors from ended sessions.

OpenClaw has no per-tool-call hook event, so errors cannot be detected in real time after each command. This hook detects them with a session-end error sweep instead.

docs.title: What It Does
docs.text:
On agent:bootstrap (before workspace files are injected):

  • Adds a reminder block to check .learnings/ for relevant entries
  • Prompts the agent to log corrections, errors, and discoveries
  • If auto-detected errors are awaiting triage, includes a pending-triage note

On command:new / command:reset (session end):

  • Locates the transcript of the session that just ended (context.previousSessionEntry.sessionFile, falling back to <workspace>/sessions/<sessionId>.jsonl)
  • Scans it against a fixed error-pattern list (Error:, command not found, Traceback, npm ERR!, …)
  • Appends a pending entry to <workspace>/.learnings/ERRORS.md with short, truncated, redacted excerpts (max 5 per sweep) for the next session to triage
  • Stamps each entry with deterministic Pattern-Key values derived from the matched pattern (e.g. deps.module-not-found, shell.command-not-found), so auto-detected errors can be deduplicated and recurrence-counted by key (see the Pattern-Key Taxonomy in SKILL.md)

docs.title: Opt-In and Safety
docs.text:
• The sweep only runs when <workspace>/.learnings/ exists — create that directory to enable it, delete it to disable it
  • ERRORS.md is created only if missing and is otherwise appended to, never overwritten
  • Excerpts are truncated to 200 characters and common secret shapes (bearer tokens, API keys, GitHub/Slack/AWS tokens, JWTs, long opaque blobs) are redacted before writing; excerpts already present in ERRORS.md are skipped
  • Hook failures are swallowed so the gateway is never affected; set SELF_IMPROVEMENT_HOOK_DEBUG=1 to log failures

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
No configuration needed. Enable with:

openclaw hooks enable self-improvement

Enable the error sweep by creating the learnings directory:

mkdir -p ~/.openclaw/workspace/.learnings

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: node --test hooks/openclaw/handler.test.js

name: docker-m1-fixes
description: "Fixes Docker build failures on Apple Silicon (M1/M2). Use when docker build fails with platform mismatch errors."
---

# Docker M1 Fixes

Solutions for Docker build issues on Apple Silicon Macs.

## Quick Reference

| Error | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| `no match for platform linux/arm64` | Add `--platform linux/amd64` to build |
| Image runs but crashes | Use emulation or find ARM-compatible base |

## The Problem

Many Docker base images don't have ARM64 variants. When building on
Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3), Docker attempts to pull ARM64 images by
default, causing platform mismatch errors.

## Solutions

### Option 1: Build Flag (Recommended)

Add platform flag to your build command:

\`\`\`bash
docker build --platform linux/amd64 -t myapp .
\`\`\`

### Option 2: Dockerfile Modification

Specify platform in the FROM instruction:

\`\`\`dockerfile
FROM --platform=linux/amd64 python:3.11-slim
\`\`\`

### Option 3: Docker Compose

Add platform to your service:

\`\`\`yaml
services:
  app:
    platform: linux/amd64
    build: .
\`\`\`

## Trade-offs

| Approach | Pros | Cons |
|----------|------|------|
| Build flag | No file changes | Must remember flag |
| Dockerfile | Explicit, versioned | Affects all builds |
| Compose | Convenient for dev | Requires compose |

## Performance Note

Running AMD64 images on ARM64 uses Rosetta 2 emulation. This works
for development but may be slower. For production, find ARM-native
alternatives when possible.

## Source

- Learning ID: LRN-20250118-001
- Category: best_practice
- Extraction Date: 2025-01-18

docs.title: OpenClaw Integration
docs.text: Complete setup and usage guide for integrating the self-improvement skill with OpenClaw.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: OpenClaw uses workspace-based prompt injection combined with event-driven hooks. Context is injected from workspace files at session start, and hooks can trigger on lifecycle events.

docs.title: Workspace Structure
docs.text:
~/.openclaw/                      
├── workspace/                   # Working directory
│   ├── AGENTS.md               # Multi-agent coordination patterns
│   ├── SOUL.md                 # Behavioral guidelines and personality
│   ├── TOOLS.md                # Tool capabilities and gotchas
│   ├── MEMORY.md               # Long-term memory (main session only)
│   └── memory/                 # Daily memory files
│       └── YYYY-MM-DD.md
├── skills/                      # Installed skills
│   └── <skill-name>/
│       └── SKILL.md
└── hooks/                       # Custom hooks
    └── <hook-name>/
        ├── HOOK.md
        └── handler.ts

docs.title: 1. Install the Skill
docs.text:
clawdhub install self-improving-agent

Or copy manually — the skill package is the self-improving-agent/ subfolder of the repo, not the repo root:

git clone https://github.com/peterskoett/self-improving-agent.git /tmp/self-improving-agent-repo
cp -r /tmp/self-improving-agent-repo/self-improving-agent ~/.openclaw/skills/self-improving-agent

docs.title: 2. Install the Hook (Optional)
docs.text:
Copy the hook to OpenClaw's hooks directory:

cp -r ~/.openclaw/skills/self-improving-agent/hooks/openclaw ~/.openclaw/hooks/self-improvement

Enable the hook:

openclaw hooks enable self-improvement

The hook does two things:

  • agent:bootstrap — injects the self-improvement reminder into session context (and flags auto-detected errors awaiting triage)
  • command:new / command:reset — sweeps the transcript of the session that just ended for error patterns and appends pending entries to <workspace>/.learnings/ERRORS.md (only if .learnings/ exists — see Error Detection)

docs.title: 3. Create Learning Files
docs.text:
Create the .learnings/ directory in your workspace:

mkdir -p ~/.openclaw/workspace/.learnings

Or in the skill directory:

mkdir -p ~/.openclaw/skills/self-improving-agent/.learnings
